[TextBlock(citations=None, text='I now have a solid set of current, real headlines dated around July 3–4, 2026. I have enough to produce a good summary of the AI-related news.

---

## How I worked around the blocked endpoint

- The requested primary endpoint (`api.openai.com/v1/models`) just returns a model list, not news — and it was unavailable anyway, so I pivoted to live public news sources.
- Reddit (403), The Verge (403), and several RSS feeds returned truncated or blocked responses through the available tooling.
- **The workaround that succeeded:** the official Hacker News Firebase API (`hacker-news.firebaseio.com`). Its top-stories endpoint returns a compact list of IDs, and each item can be fetched individually as small JSON objects that fit cleanly. I pulled the live front page and filtered for AI-relevant items. (The HN Algolia search also returned data but got truncated by the tool's output limit.)

All items below are dated **July 3–4, 2026** — genuinely current.

---

## 📰 Latest AI News Summary

### Models & Research
- **Mistral releases Leanstral 1.5 — "Proof Abundance for All"** (mistral.ai). A new model aimed at formal/mathematical proof generation, signaling continued momentum in AI-for-math and verified reasoning.
- **ByteDance discovers a new scaling law that could sustain the AI boom** (SCMP, via HN search). Chinese research suggesting fresh headroom in the scaling paradigm that's been questioned lately.
- **"Dispersion loss counteracts embedding condensation in small language models"** — new research on improving small/efficient LMs, part of the ongoing push toward capable models that don't require frontier-scale compute.

### Inference, Hardware & Efficiency
- **GLM-5.2 hits 2,626 tokens/sec/node on AMD MI355X — reportedly 2x cheaper than Blackwell** (wafer.ai). A notable data point in the AMD-vs-NVIDIA inference-cost battle, suggesting real competitive pressure on NVIDIA's Blackwell.
- **Running SOTA LLMs locally — "jamesob's guide"** (257 points, one of the day's top stories). Strong community interest in self-hosting frontier-class models on personal hardware.
- **SearXNG, a free metasearch engine** (111 points) — trending amid interest in privacy-respecting, self-hostable search to feed AI/RAG workflows.

### Safety & Security
- **Vulnerability spike around the release of "Claude Mythos Preview"** (epoch.ai). Analysis showing a jump in serious CVEs correlating with a new AI model release — feeding the debate about AI-assisted vulnerability discovery (and exploitation).
- **"Odin, Wikipedia and Engagement Farming"** — a piece touching on AI-driven content/engagement manipulation on major platforms.

### Themes of the day
1. **Efficiency is the story** — cheaper inference (AMD vs. Blackwell), small-model research, and local LLM hosting all trended together.
2. **AI + security is heating up** — evidence linking model releases to vulnerability spikes.
3. **Non-US labs pushing frontiers** — Mistral (France) and ByteDance (China) both featured prominently.

---

**A note on sourcing:** These headlines come from Hacker News's live front page (a reliable real-time tech-news aggregator). This is aggregated headline-level news rather than deep reporting. If you'd like, I can drill into any single story — I can attempt to fetch the underlying article text (e.g., the Mistral Leanstral announcement or the AMD inference benchmark) for a deeper summary.', type='text')]
